function: p. 6: SAC deep reinforcement learning jointly sets RIS deployment positions, panel azimuth angles and reflecting coefficients (phase shifts) to maximize network ergodic capacity.
system: p. 2-4, 8: multi-BS (E-antenna ULA), single-antenna UEs, J hybrid active-passive reflecting RISs (N-element UPA, 25% active), near-field; mmWave cited, no carrier frequency stated.
method: p. 6-8: Soft actor-critic (actor, two Q-networks, value and target networks, replay buffer); reinforcement learning in a simulated network; reward is approximate ergodic capacity (Eq. 19).
data_channel: p. 3-5, 8: custom simulator, near-field Rician channels (spherical-wave LoS plus Rayleigh NLoS), random 200x200 m layout with random obstacles; no dataset or measurements.
test_conditions: p. 7-8: SAC trains in the simulated 200x200 m region and the found deployment is evaluated there (J=4/8, M=32/16, K=5-30 dB); p. 10: MRT/ZF/MMSE precoders, 5-15% CSI error.
baselines: p. 8: Exhaustive search, DDPG [34], uniform random [9], RISs near BSs [8], near UEs, PPP [10]; passive and active RIS for energy efficiency (p. 10).
metrics: p. 8-10: ergodic capacity (bit/s/Hz), running time (min), approximation error (%), convergence steps, energy efficiency (bits/Joule/Hz).
complexity: p. 7, 9: O(Epo T B sum U_i U_{i-1}) for SAC training; Table II runtime 21.53 min (proposal), 17.12 (DDPG), 33266.58 (exhaustive search).
q1_support: p. 3: "the Rician channel model is employed to characterize the BS-RIS and RIS-UE links [23]". Custom near-field Rician plus Rayleigh simulator; no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 8: "Unless otherwise specified, the first parameter mentioned above is the default value." Settings are only swept (J, M, E, N, K, SNR, CSI error); no statement that a trained policy is applied to an unseen scenario. Fig. 10 (p. 10) tests other precoders on the found deployment only.
q3_support: p. 8: "(2) The deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm [34] is employed to optimize RISs deployment" is the learned baseline; "(1) Exhaustive search for optimal RISs deployment" and "(3) Uniform random RISs deployment [9]" are non-learned; all compared on ergodic capacity in Fig. 6 (p. 9).
q4_support: p. 7: "complexity of the optimization algorithm is O(Epo(T B(" for the SAC training; p. 9: "requiring 21.5 minutes on a system with an Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700" and Table II running times.
q5_support: p. 8: "the UEs are randomly scattered in the area by setting a clustering factor of 0.3" shows a synthetic setup; no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere in the paper (the only URL is the IEEE rights notice, p. 1).
notes: Included under area 3: the SAC action includes the RIS reflecting coefficients (phase shifts) jointly with RIS placement and orientation (p. 6, Eq. 25), so the above_phy exclusion for placement does not apply. Fig. 10 (p. 10) evaluates the deployment optimized with the MRT-based capacity approximation (Eq. 19) under MRT, ZF and MMSE precoders; q2 is not marked because the paper never states that the SAC was trained on one precoder and tested on another, or on unseen users, antennas or channel models. The reviewer may reconsider q2 on that figure.
